title: NGC 7727’s spectacular galactic dance as seen by the VLT
caption: The merged galaxy NGC 7727, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: NGC 7727 · constellation Aquarius · about 90 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: The galaxy NGC 7727 has a wispy shape, the result of two galaxies merging. Their merger began around a billion years ago, and NGC 7727 is what the pair has become.

When galaxies merge, their gravity pulls stars and gas out of their original orbits, leaving loose, irregular structures like the wisps around this one. Each large galaxy is thought to hold a supermassive black hole at its center, and a merger brings those black holes together too.

That is happening deep inside NGC 7727. Two supermassive black holes are spiralling toward each other in the galaxy's core. They are expected to merge within 250 million years. That sounds like a long wait, but on the timescales that galaxies live by, it is very short. The galaxy lies about 90 million light-years away, and this picture comes from the FORS2 instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope (VLT).
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (7.24 x 7.19 arcminutes) and distance (90 million light years), the frame spans roughly 190,000 × 188,000 light-years. Its light set out about 90 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The FORS2 instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope recorded NGC 7727 in visible light through blue, green and red filters. The color mapping isn't published.
filters: 440 nm · Optical B (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
557 nm · Optical V (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
655 nm · Optical R (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
understand.eye: The VLT's large mirror and long exposures gather far more light than the eye, which is why faint wisps around the galaxy show up.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: FORS2 stands for FOcal Reducer and low dispersion Spectrograph 2. For this picture it recorded the galaxy through three visible-light filters, centered on blue, green and red wavelengths of 440, 557 and 655 nanometers.
alt: A galaxy with a wispy, irregular shape formed by the merger of two galaxies.
